findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_board.py `_ancestor_merge_problem` computes `own = base..refs/heads/<branch>` and compares it with `--first-parent base..main`. If the branch is fast-forwarded to main (reconcile does this), `own` contains the second-parent commits of every `--no-ff` merge that landed on main after registration. Those commits are not on main's first-parent line, so `any(commit not in first_parent ...)` is true and the result is `merged-branch`. The design (case 5) and the spec scenario both assume every commit since registration lies on the first-parent line in this case. The test `test_unproven_merges_are_kept_with_named_reasons` only advances main with linear commits, so it does not cover this. The fresh-task data-loss bug is therefore still reachable on repositories that merge PRs with merge commits.
findings.summary: A commitless fresh task fast-forwarded to a newer main is classified `merged-branch` and removed whenever main advanced through a merge commit after registration. This contradicts the spec rule that a fast-forwarded commitless task must not be classified merged.
